findings_qualitative.value: Molecular gas is disturbed with no rotationally supported structure; 80% within central 5 kpc, remainder in a 20 kpc filament

evidence.quote: The molecular gas morphology is complex and disturbed, showing no evidence for a rotationally-supported structure in equilibrium.

claims.hypothesis: Is the molecular gas condensed from the hot atmosphere rather than supplied by mergers or stripping?
claims.experiment: Compared condensation, cooling time and mass budget with merger/stripping alternatives
claims.result: Condensation can supply 1.9e10 Msun in 2.4e8 yr, matching the cooling time
claims.finding: Gas likely condensed from the ICM

evidence.quote: The cold gas has likely condensed out of the hot atmosphere.

claims.hypothesis: Did the putative X-ray cavity stimulate the filament's formation?
claims.experiment: Chandra residual image, cavity energetics, displaced mass versus filament mass
claims.result: Cavity displaced ~1e10 Msun but filament lies along its edge, not behind it
claims.finding: Energetically feasible but morphology less conclusive

evidence.quote: This is enegetically feasible, although the morphology is not as conclusive as systems whose molecular filaments trail directly behind buoyant radio bubbles.

claims.experiment: Fit Hernquist free-fall model to the PV curve
claims.result: Requires inclination within ~20 deg of the plane of the sky

evidence.quote: It is only consistent with free-fall if it lies within $20^{\circ}$ of the plane of the sky.

claims.hypothesis: Does star formation follow the Kennicutt-Schmidt law?
claims.experiment: Fit Sigma_SFR vs Sigma_H2 in regions
claims.result: Central gas consistent with KS; filament has higher Sigma_SFR
claims.finding: Core consistent with KS; filament elevated, possibly gas consumption or varying X_CO

evidence.quote: Star formation near the cluster core is consistent with the Kennicutt-Schmidt law.

why_this_method.value: Galactic X_CO adopted as standard practice until direct calibrations in BCGs exist

evidence.quote: We continue to follow the standard practice of adopting the Galactic $X_{\rm CO}$ until more direct calibrations in BCGs are available.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Mergers, tidal stripping and ram pressure stripping rejected as gas sources

evidence.quote: minor mergers, tidal stripping, and ram pressure stripping are all unlikely to be viable mechanisms for supplying the rich reservoir of cold gas in BCGs.

limitations_admitted.value: The cavity is poorly defined and may not be real

evidence.quote: The feature identified as a potential cavity is poorly defined, so it is not clear if it is a real cavity.

limitations_admitted.value: HST images manually aligned, so small-scale offsets between gas and UV may be missed

evidence.quote: Spatial offsets between the molecular gas and young stars could be present, but would be missed due to this manual alignment.

referee_caveats_inferred: X_CO uncertainty (factor of a few) propagates to masses and KS conclusions
Local SFRs rely on scaling a single global SFR by UV counts with no local extinction correction
Free-fall model is simplistic; fit uncertainties on inclination not given
ALMA recovers only 45% of single-dish flux, so extended gas is missed
